Local-runs: probe — the skills ratchet family (`node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` on the head worktree and on a detached worktree at the base `27e0bd584`, `node scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, `node scripts/pm/check-skill-id-lint.mjs`, `node scripts/check-skill-identifier-liveness.mjs`, `pnpm check:doc-anchors`, `node scripts/check-docs-section-name.mjs`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec run check:skill-docs` and `check:skill-refs`, and `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 28170`) was executed locally, because the one gate this diff can turn red is a per-file token count that the dev paid down to a headroom of 0 and 5 and no check-run prints as a number; `check:docs` and `check:doc-formula-expressions` stopped at a prerequisite (exit 1 for a missing `packages/spec/json-schema`, exit 3 for an unbuilt `@objectstack/formula`) and are NOT MEASURED here, read from CI; nothing else was built or run.

Inputs: `git diff 27e0bd584..f2cd1d931` (3 files, +27 / −23, one commit, author `Claude`, trailers `Co-authored-by` and `Claude-Session` present, no model name, no `Refs`); `git merge-base pr-28170 origin/main` is `27e0bd584`; `origin/main` had moved eight commits to `9f13ee815` at review time and none of them touches the three files, `connector-nodes.ts` or `scripts/pm`; the PR body and its one comment (6526073574, the contract-review claim naming this session and this head; no reviews, no hold, no hand-off); card #28041 (body; triage 6521031879 and 6524854844; claim 6525243871); PR #28035 (body, 5-file list, merged 2026-10-30T12:13Z as `ec7e15abc`, an ancestor of the base; its contract review 6520142501 whose ①1 and ①3 findings the merged code answers); #27968 (open, `pm:dispatched`, `domain:spec`); PR #28150 (open, ready, not draft, not merged, head `6a06a420b`, `Fixes #27968`, its 22-file list carries no `skills/**` path); card #28162 (open, `pm:blocked` on #28150); the dispatch order and the dev report at /mnt/project-files/skills-lane-seat2/; .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md and review-checklist.md; the code at `origin/main` for every claim the new sentences make; the head's check-runs (three polls, last at 2026-10-30T15:18Z).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set: unchanged — correct.** The diff is prose only: two governed skill files and one docs page. No schema, export, type or runtime behaviour moves; `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` hold. The register reads 2 of 3 paths as `skills/**`, Tier H, 50 changed lines under the human-merge threshold; the reading is the dev's.
2. **What is judged — the new text names the shipped subset exactly.** `collectInputSchemaViolations` (`connector-nodes.ts` :248-298) judges `required` (the object's own `required` list, a missing or `undefined` key), `type` (a string or a type list, every member in `JUDGED_TYPES`, else unjudged; `integer` is `Number.isInteger` or a bigint; `nullable: true` admits null, :257), `properties` (descent, :288-293) and `items` (descent by index, :295-296). The row's "`required`, `type`, `properties`, `items`", the recipe's "`type` (with OpenAPI `nullable`)" and the docs row's "a missing `required` parameter, a wrong `type`" are that list. Everything outside the subset (`$ref`, combinators, `enum`, `format`, bounds, `additionalProperties`) never refuses, and the new text claims nothing about it.
3. **When — "once evaluated ... before dispatch" is the code's order.** `resolveValueSlotMap` (:124) runs first, the judgment (:138-143) next, `handler(input, handlerCtx)` (:168) only on an empty violation list. The pins `sent` being `[]` in every refusal test. "Nothing sent" / "nothing is sent" is true, and the shipped message says it in the same words ("Nothing was sent.", :154).
4. **The code and its routing — right.** The result is `{ success: false, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', error }` (:147-150) with no `errorClass`, and `NodeExecutionResult.errorClass` "defaults to `runtime`" (`engine.ts` :401-407; the `NodeFailureClass` docblock: "A declared `fault` edge routes it"). The test pins a `fault` edge receiving `$error.code === 'VALIDATION_ERROR'` (:154-161, :193-199). "`fault`-routable" in both skill files and "a `fault` edge or `try_catch` can route it" in the docs row are true.
5. **`null` on an optional parameter counts as absent — right, and the recipe says exactly that.** :291 `if (record[key] === null && !required.has(key)) continue;`, pinned at test :248. The recipe's "`null` on an optional parameter is absent" is this line; a `null` on a REQUIRED parameter is still refused (:216-221), and the recipe does not say otherwise.
6. **Text is never converted; the CEL cast is `int()` — right spelling.** :261-263 sets `textForScalar` when a string meets `integer`, `number` or `boolean`, and the message then appends the cast prescription naming `int()`, `double()` or `bool()` (:159-161). `int` is in the CEL standard function list (`packages/formula/src/validate.ts` :1297, `:1200`), and the merged suite at :208 pins `{"petId": int(rec.idText)}` dispatching with the number `7`. The recipe's `path: { dialect: 'cel', source: '{"petId": int(record.vendor_id)}' }` is that pinned shape with the record field renamed; the docs row's "cast it in a CEL envelope (`int()`, `double()`, `bool()`)" is the message's own list.
7. **Naming each path — right.** Lines are `missing required 'path.petId'` (with the required children of a missing section, :275-281) and `'query.verbose' must be boolean, got string` (:260), capped at `MAX_NAMED_VIOLATIONS = 5` then "; and N more". The recipe's "naming each path" and the docs row's "naming each parameter path" are true; neither claims the cap, which is fine.
8. **Quoted message text — the PR body quotes it verbatim; the diff quotes none of it.** The PR body's message (with NODE, CONNECTOR and ACTION placeholders) is the template at :151-161 character for character, including "does not match the action's inputSchema —", "Nothing was sent.", "Fix connectorConfig.input so it satisfies the inputSchema GET /api/v1/automation/connectors lists for this action." and the cast sentence. The three files quote only the code `VALIDATION_ERROR` and the route `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors`, both verbatim.
9. **"`os validate` does not judge it yet" — true today, imprecise, and the one must-fix (the coordinator's question (a)).** On `origin/main` neither door judges `connectorConfig.input` at all: #27968 is open, so a literal `input: {}` for `getPet` registers and validates and is refused only at run time (PR #28035 body, inventory 4). Two different checks are in play, and the diff's sentence does not say which one it means:
   - **#28035 (merged):** the evaluated input against the action's `inputSchema` — a shape check, run time only. Nothing in the repo judges it at registration or `os validate`, and PR #28150 does not add that (its describe text, ledger entry and both new test files judge envelope well-formedness and template tokens; a well-formed literal that breaks the schema still registers).
   - **#28150 (open, ready):** the value slot's envelope — a malformed CEL envelope, a template envelope, a `{…}` token — refused at `connectorConfig.input.KEY` by `registerFlow` and `os validate`. That is the check the old sentence's consequence clause ("so a malformed envelope fails at run time") described, and the clause the diff rightly drops.
   The diff's SKILL.md row ("`os validate` does not judge it yet"), the recipe ("`os validate` does not judge it yet", after the cast example) and the docs row ("`os validate` does not judge the input yet") all leave the antecedent open. Read as the schema check they stay true after #28150; read as the map or the input they turn false the moment #28150 lands — and #28150 is ready while this PR waits on a Tier H approver, so the landing order is not in the seat's hands, and "true on main at merge time" cannot be promised for the open spelling. #28162 covers SKILL.md:88 and the recipe :18-21 but not the connectors.mdx row. Fix: name the check — "`os validate` does not judge the `inputSchema` fit yet" (or "... does not check the input against the `inputSchema` yet") in all three places. Order-independent, three to five tokens; SKILL.md has 5 tokens of headroom, the recipe needs one more same-file cut (see should-fix 1 for a candidate), the docs page is unpriced. Must-fix 1.
10. **The restatement cuts — restatement, each with a surviving home, one `why` lost.** Read sentence by sentence on the head:
   - SKILL.md `approval` row "(from `plugin-approvals`)": the `requires` table :341 says `approvals` → `approval` / `approval_revise` (`plugin-approvals`). Kept.
   - SKILL.md § Integrations "never an `http` node holding a credential": the `http` row :86 says "never a credential there: a credential means a declared connector called via `connector_action`". Kept.
   - SKILL.md null-operand bullet "(not `fault`-routable)": the ROUTES table :141 lists "filter operand that evaluated to `null`" under "Does NOT route (fatal either way)". Kept.
   - SKILL.md "`notify` delivers, `connector_action` reaches a vendor, a function computes": the node rows and the PURE-compute paragraph :249 carry each clause. Kept.
   - Recipe 1 "trimming still keeps the package small": recipe 1's comment :39-40 prescribes the trim ("Trim the vendor's OpenAPI 3.x document to the operations the app calls and ship it in the package"). The prescription is kept; the size rationale is a `why`, not a rule.
   - Recipe 4 "// an inbound post carries no trigger user": `runAs: 'system'` stays on the `api` flow :111, and recipe 1 :49 teaches "a scheduled run has no trigger user". The prescription is kept; the `api`-flow reason now has no home (should-fix 2).
   - Recipe 4 "// never a literal secret": the intro :10-11 ("an `api` flow's hook secret goes to the deployment and to the sender") and the `secretRef` key itself. Kept.
   - Recipe 5 "// inline OpenAPI 3.x": the next line spells `openapi: '3.0.3'` inline. Kept.
   - The OAuth bullet's "Declare the connector, fields and flows, mark the integration **blocked** ..., and say so": the section heading :149 "Not yet — declare the rest, mark the integration blocked, write no plugin" is the rule; the bullet keeps "Blocked on the platform's outbound-OAuth card". Kept.
   - "with its input schema, visible" after recipe 5: Holds bullet 2 now carries the schema and its judgment. Kept.
11. **Eval corpus — the dev's deviation names the wrong line; the real stale rubric is older than this PR (should-fix 3).** `evals/integrations-declared.json` nowhere contains "trimming still keeps the package small"; eval 1's rubric says "a trimmed, packaged OpenAPI 3.x document", which recipe 1 still teaches, so that cut breaks nothing. What eval 1's `expected_output` does say is "`connectorConfig.input` is sent as written, so a per-contract payload waits on the platform too" — false on `main` since #27327 (a CEL envelope is evaluated) and now contradicted by the recipe's own sentence ("kept as written ... judged ... before dispatch"). It is a rubric line, not a `must_contain` token (those are `defineConnector`, `provider: 'openapi'`, `credentialRef`, `connector_action`, `type: 'api'`, `secretRef`, `Swagger 2.0`, `blocked`, all still taught), so grading by tokens is unaffected; a rubric-reading grader is steered to reward a stale claim. Pre-existing, outside the surface, not caused by this diff — a follow-up, not a must-fix. In the same rubric, "the `openapi` provider has no `include` key, so the trimmed document is the allowlist" contradicts recipe 1 on `main` (:70-72, `providerConfig.include` allowlists operation keys); same carrier.
12. **Ratchets and lint hold on the head.** `check-skills-token-ratchet`: SKILL.md 6457 → 6452 of 6457 (headroom 5), integration-recipes.md 2236 → 2236 of 2236 (headroom 0); the base worktree reads 6457 and 2236, so the dev's before/after numbers are exact and no ceiling moved (`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in the diff). `check-skill-line-ratchet` exit 0; `check-skill-id-lint` 105 files clean; `check-skill-identifier-liveness` OK (486 citations); `check:doc-anchors` 832 fragment links resolve; `check-docs-section-name` exit 0; `check:skill-docs` and `check:skill-refs` in sync; `check-doc-route-spelling --advisory` clean (the docs row's `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors` spells the ledger row). `Check Documentation Links` is success on the head.
13. **The connectors.mdx row fits the table.** "Failure modes at a glance" is a two-column table (`You wrote / it happened` | `What you get`); the new row has two cells and the pipe count of its neighbours. It sits between the "Wrong spec URL" row and the "runtime reload" row; the table's preamble frames boot-time faults, but the reload row already carries a non-boot case, so a run-time refusal row is in character (④ notes the placement).
14. **Consistency elsewhere.** `git grep` on `origin/main` over `skills/**`, `content/docs/**` and `docs/adr/**` for "sent as written", "as written", "does not judge", "unchecked", "inputSchema" finds no third sentence that calls the input unchecked: the only two are the ones this diff rewrites. `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` :146 ("Declared input parameter types, for Studio form generation and runtime validation") now reads true rather than aspirational. Outside the three faces, `packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts` :950 ("handed to the action as written: no template is read there") and PR #28150's rewritten describe text ("Each value is a literal, handed to the action as written, or a CEL value envelope ...") speak of template interpolation, not of the schema check; they are not false, and they are #28150's and #28162's, not this PR's.
15. **PR body declarations.** `Fixes #28041` on its own line; no closing keyword beside any other open card number (#27968 and #28162 appear only as plain references — #28162 does not appear at all). `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, six `## 维护者速读` lines with the last saying a contract review is owed, Tier H, a governed approver. Labels `documentation`, `size/s`, `skip-changeset`; author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; draft; base `main`. The shipped message is quoted in the body verbatim (①.8).

### ② Semver level

No release. `skip-changeset` is right: no published package's `files[]` ships `skills/**` or `content/docs/**` (the skills catalog is governed, not packaged), `dispatch-gates` derived no changeset family, and the `Check Changeset` check-run is success on this head. `Clause-②: no` is right: no narrowing is declared or present, and the narrowing this text documents (PR #28035) carried its own `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags: no `open_questions`. Three declared deviations: (1) the commit amended once to drop a `Fixes` line — the trailer check passes and the card relation lives in the PR body, accepted; (2) the eval rubric note — the line it names does not exist, the line that is stale is older than this PR (①.11, should-fix 3), accepted as a flag with the correction recorded here; (3) SKILL.md's ceiling not re-locked at 6452 — the ratchet is shrink-only and the script is outside the surface, accepted; the next SKILL.md editor may lower the pin.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 NOT MEASURED (question (4)): the gate loads every published `require` entry point from `dist/` (`scripts/check-dual-build-cjs-loads.mjs` header, #12971); a docs-and-skills diff touches no source, no `exports` map and no build config, so it cannot change the gate's answer. CI hosts it in `Build Core` (`ci.yml` :2998), which is in the head's run population (success at the last poll). The NOT MEASURED is honest and immaterial.
- Coordinator's questions, answered: (a) different checks — the sentence must name the `inputSchema` fit (①.9, must-fix 1). (b) #28150 touches no `skills/**` or `content/docs/automation/**` file, so the two PRs cannot conflict in git; #28162's future PR rewrites the same SKILL.md:88 and recipe :18-21 lines that this PR rewrites, so #28162 must start from `main` after this PR lands and keep the schema sentences — carry that note onto #28162 (should-fix 4). (c) Go in now: the schema check, its code, routing, the null rule and the cast, all true on `main` today and after #28150; plus the sharpened `os validate` clause of must-fix 1, true in either landing order. Wait for #28162: any sentence saying what `os validate` DOES judge (envelope, template token) — false until #28150 merges, and triage 6525897453 says do not edit before the merge.
- Independence: the diff was produced by `session_016WV4cwp1Wc6nB6ePmS4ePn` on `claude/project-thread-bcip5d` (the card thread's platform-assigned branch, the recorded exception the claim names); this record is rendered by `session_016WV4d1QkPVVzNz3FJqb2iS`, which did not draft it. The claim comment 6526073574 names this session and this head; no competing claim, hold or hand-off; no reviews on the PR.
- Author: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no non-bot login to record.
- Tier: H by the register (`skills/**` ×2); the maintainer or a GOVERNED_APPROVERS review lands it. Draft PR; nothing to disarm.
- CI (48 check-runs on the head, last poll 2026-10-30T15:21Z): 30 success, 17 skipped by path or design, 0 failure, 1 in progress (`Test Core (1/8)`). Success includes both required jobs (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `Type Check · source gates`/`workspace`/`debt ledger`/`consumer gates`) and `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, the three `Lint · scoped` jobs, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `(3/8)`, `Test UI`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Check Changeset`, `Auto Label`, `Spec property liveness`, `Live E2E UI`, `filter`. Skipped: the UI build, lint, type-check and test shards, Build UI Deps, Temporal Conformance, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, the opt-in harnesses, the schedule gate. The landing seat re-reads the one in-progress run before the ready flip.
- Not re-run here: the dev's 60 dispatch-gates families (read from the report; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` is success on this head); the service-automation suite (the pins were read, not executed); `check:docs` and `check:doc-formula-expressions` (prerequisite, CI's).

### ④ Design judgment

Rules face, the two skill files, against the code they cite and the scenario they are accepted against (an AI author wiring a `connector_action` over an OpenAPI action with a required integer parameter held as text):

- **SKILL.md :88 — holds against the code; one clause imprecise (must-fix 1).** The row now teaches the author the four judged keywords, the failure code, that a `fault` edge can catch it and that nothing reaches the vendor — each anchored to a line of `connector-nodes.ts`. The row stays one line, within its table, and 5 tokens under the ceiling; nothing it dropped was a rule. The `os validate` clause is the only sentence whose truth depends on the landing order of an open PR.
- **integration-recipes.md Holds bullet 2 — holds; the cast example is the pinned one.** "kept as written" over "sent as written" is the exact correction the #28035 review asked for (its `Skills-docs` line, "sent as written" falsified); the bullet then gives the author the one thing the error message cannot — the CEL spelling before the first run — and the shape is the merged test's own (:208). `null`-on-optional is the #28035 review's ①1 must-fix, now on `main` and now taught; the cast is its ①3, now the shipped prescription. The eval prompts (DocuSign, Stripe, legacy ERP) still resolve to the same recipes; eval 1's rubric is the stale piece (①.11), not the recipe.
- **connectors.mdx row (prose face, the seat's ACCEPT; read for ④ because the governed sentences point at it).** Code, routing, remedy and listing route are the message's; it is the only place a human reader learns the remedy list. Placement under a boot-faults preamble is tolerable given the reload row; an editor may one day split run-time rows out. Its `os validate` clause is the one site #28162 does not cover (must-fix 1).
- **The restatement cuts as a method.** Paying for a rule with same-file restatement is what the ratchet exists to force, and every removed sentence has a surviving prescription (①.10). The one real loss is a `why` (recipe 4's `runAs` reason), carried as should-fix 2 because the ratchet leaves no room for it today.
- **Cited code was read to judge the prose, not reviewed.** Nothing in `connector-nodes.ts` or the test file is under review here.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-bcip5d`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1QkPVVzNz3FJqb2iS`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Must-fix:
1. (this PR, all three files) Name the check `os validate` does not perform, so the sentence is true whether #28150 lands before or after this PR: SKILL.md :88 "`os validate` does not judge the `inputSchema` fit yet", the recipe's last sentence of Holds bullet 2 the same, and the connectors.mdx row "`os validate` does not judge the input against the `inputSchema` yet". SKILL.md has 5 tokens of headroom; the recipe has 0 and needs one more same-file restatement cut of three to five tokens, chosen by the dev on the same rule as the others (a restatement whose prescription survives elsewhere in the file, named in the PR body) and not a rule such as the OAuth bullet's `bearer`-ref sentence or an answer shape; the docs page is unpriced. A delta review on the new head by the same reviewer closes it.

Should-fix:
1. (this PR, if the recipe cut for must-fix 1 lands near it) Keep "(`{…}`, `{{ }}` are literal text)" in Holds bullet 2 untouched: it is true today and is the exact clause #28162 rewrites after #28150; cutting it now would hand #28162 a different base.
2. (carrier: #28162, which already reopens the recipe) Restore the `api`-flow `runAs` reason in recipe 4 in two or three words ("no trigger user") when #28162 next spends tokens there; today only the scheduled-run reason in recipe 1 survives.
3. (carrier: #28162, widen its scope by one file) `skills/objectstack-automation/evals/integrations-declared.json` eval 1 `expected_output`: replace "`connectorConfig.input` is sent as written, so a per-contract payload waits on the platform too" with the value-slot plus schema-check truth (a per-contract payload is a CEL envelope, judged against the action's `inputSchema` before dispatch), and drop "the `openapi` provider has no `include` key" (recipe 1 teaches `providerConfig.include`). Rubric lines only; the `must_contain` tokens stay. Evals are not priced (#27984).
4. (carrier: #28162, a note on the card) #28162's PR must start from `main` after this PR lands and keep bullet 2's schema sentences; it changes only the `os validate` and template-token clauses. PR #28150 itself touches no skills file, so there is no git conflict between #28150 and this PR.
5. (carrier: the dev report's next edition, no code) The report's deviation 2 names a phrase the eval does not contain; the stale rubric line is the one in should-fix 3. Recorded here so the seat's ACCEPT does not repeat it.
